anita: Heads-up — we're seeing a p99 latency spike on prod-g5x around 10:12 UTC for short-seq traffic (seq_len <= 64). Baseline 45ms -> 120ms. Traces point to a kernel choice flip after the 535.12 driver rollout :eyes:

mike: confirmed on the same host pool. Detector shows a sudden increase in flash->fallback kernel fallthroughs. I captured a short perf log.

mike: ```
2026-03-18T10:12:14Z host=g5x-07 model=redwood-7b seq=32
selector: candidate_kernels=[flash_attn_v2, aten_flash, cu_backprop_fallback]
chosen_kernel=aten_flash (fallback path)
kv_cache_hit_rate=0.87 -> 0.52
batching.avg_batch_size=4.2 -> 1.9
latency.p99=45ms -> 118ms
```

sasha: looks like selector scoring changed — maybe driver API made flash kernels return different workspace/query flags so autoselect prefers aten. Also seeing more KV cache evictions which reduces batching effectiveness.

lucas: I pulled the kernel selector traces. Triton autoselect returned lower score for flash on tensorcore path because workspace_query failed for small seq. snippet:```
TRITON_SELECTOR: kernel=flash_attn_v2 score=0.42 workspace_ok=false
TRITON_SELECTOR: kernel=aten_flash score=0.86 workspace_ok=true
```

anita: KV thrash explanation makes sense — when the kernel flips we rebuild execution plan and evict KV more frequently, short seq workloads pay a lot. Is this reproducible on canary?

runtime-ci: canary run started against canary-g5x pool with driver pinned to 534.89 (pre-rollout). Will compare.

mike: quick repro: forcing kernel via env override restores p99. set MODEL_KERNEL_OVERRIDE=flash_attn_v2 on a single node and ran 5k requests. p99 back to 48ms.

sasha: temporary mitigation = force kernel for short-seq models + disable the new driver on critical pools. Longer-term: update selector workspace probe to handle new driver semantics and add a fast-path for short seqs to prefer flash even if workspace_query is conservative.

anita: posting perf dashboards: https://dash.redwood.internal/d/rt/p99-g5x?from=now-1h to #eng-runtime for visibility.

deploy-bot: Canary with 534.89 driver shows no spike; comparing traces now — ETA 10m.

lucas: creating a small patch to selector: treat workspace_ok=false as "maybe" for seq<=64 and add fallback_score_bonus for flash kernels. Will open PR and run unit selector tests.

anita: action items:
- mike: keep kernel override on affected nodes (hotfix) :thumbsup:
- lucas: PR for selector heuristic change, include regression test with new driver (due today EOD)
- sasha: coord with infra to roll driver back on the other 2 pools if canary confirms (hold on final rollback until CI trace diff is in)
- runtime-ci: produce a diff artifact with selector logs + KV eviction trace for postmortem

mike: quick note — we saw slight cost increase when forcing flash due to higher workspace memory for some batches, but it's within SLA tradeoff for latency-sensitive customers.

anita: good. keep updates here. If canary diffs look good we'll do a staged rollback + select kernel override removal after selector fix. :shipit:
